problems.source_says: The overlap coding omits a specific, strongly supported probable shared-sample link to c041, Effects of Personalized Generative AI on Student Creativity: Evidence from Creative Performance, Self-efficacy, and Attention Allocation (DOI 10.1007/978-981-95-4499-8_31). Both source PDFs describe 62 students, ages 18-27, with matching sex composition (c246: 41 female; c041: 33.9% male) and age summaries at different rounding precision (22.58, SD 2.53 versus 22.6, SD 2.5). They report the same two products, AI systems, crossover procedure, five-minute break and condition durations of 17 (SD 7) and 20 (SD 6) minutes. All six creativity means and SDs match exactly: standard/personalised quality 3.08 (1.12)/3.50 (1.00), elaboration 2.48 (1.04)/3.58 (1.17), and originality 3.13 (1.27)/2.92 (1.15). These primary-document matches warrant flagging c041 as a probable overlapping report before treating the papers as independent samples. The form is correct that c246 contains no explicit reuse declaration; this challenge concerns the omitted cross-document evidence, not a proven shared-person count. Neither paper explicitly confirms the identity or exact number of shared participants.
